items.title: Drug-coated balloons match DES on CV death and MI in de novo CAD: meta-analysis of 10 RCTs (eClinicalMedicine)
items.summary: Meta-analysis of 10 RCTs (7,832 patients) comparing DCB-only PCI with DES for de novo coronary disease: no difference in cardiovascular death or MI, including after excluding small-vessel-only trials. Target-lesion revascularisation was higher with DCB outside small vessels, but this signal was heterogeneous and depended on one trial.
bullets: **eClinicalMedicine meta-analysis** (PRISMA, PROSPERO-registered; searched to 30 May 2026): **drug-coated balloon (DCB-only) vs drug-eluting stent (DES)** PCI for **de novo** coronary disease.
**CV death**: OR **1.06** (0.75-1.49), I²=0%. **MI**: OR **1.02** (0.76-1.36), I²=0%. Same after excluding small-vessel-only trials.
**Excluding small-vessel-only trials**, revascularisation was **higher with DCB**: OR **1.84** (1.06-3.19), I²=54%.
That signal was **sensitive to removing one trial (REC-CAGEFREE I)**, so treat it cautiously.
Take-home: hard outcomes are **comparable**; larger vessels and complex lesions need **adequately powered, longer RCTs**. Funnel plots showed no major publication bias.

items.title: Intensive BP lowering cuts CV events 15% per 10 mm Hg with or without CKD, no rise in kidney failure (JAMA Cardiology)
items.summary: Oxford-led meta-analysis of 27 RCTs (88,830 adults): intensive vs standard BP lowering reduced major CV events by 15% per 10 mm Hg lower systolic BP, with similar relative benefit in people with and without CKD. Kidney failure was not increased, but sustained eGFR declines of 30% or more and 40% or more were, so kidney function should be monitored.
bullets: **JAMA Cardiology** systematic review and meta-analysis: **intensive vs standard BP lowering** with and without **chronic kidney disease (CKD)**.
**27 studies, 88,830 participants**; trials with ≥1 year follow-up; searched to **16 Jan 2026**; effects **standardised per 10 mm Hg** lower systolic BP.
**Major CV events fell 15% per 10 mm Hg** (RR **0.85**, 0.81-0.89), **with no difference by CKD status**.
**Absolute benefit** was **4.3 events/1000 person-years in CKD** vs **2.7 without CKD**.
**eGFR declines of ≥30% / ≥40%** were more likely: RR **1.42** and **1.47**; this did not translate into more kidney failure.
Authors: intensive BP lowering **should be recommended with or without CKD**; baseline risk is higher in CKD, so absolute gain is at least as large.
